name: Amer Sports, Inc.

profile.description: Amer Sports designs, manufactures, and distributes premium sports equipment, apparel, and footwear through iconic brands including Arc'teryx (technical apparel), Salomon (outdoor performance footwear and softgoods), Wilson (ball and racquet sports), and Peak Performance. Majority-owned by ANTA Sports, the company IPO'd on the NYSE in January 2024. Q2 2026 revenue grew 32% YoY to $1.63B with adjusted gross margin expanding 710 bps to 65.8%. FY2026 guidance raised to approximately 24% revenue growth with adjusted EPS of $1.27-$1.30. Market cap approximately $17.6B.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Arc'teryx has been transformed from a niche mountaineering brand into a global luxury-outdoor phenomenon with Technical Apparel revenue continuing to lead all segments, while Salomon crossed $2B in annual sales through expansion from ski boots into trail running and lifestyle categories [1][2]. The DTC channel reached a record 55% of Q2 revenue, representing a fundamental go-to-market transformation. AI Deployment (1/2): Amer Sports has embedded generative AI tools across productivity, content, analysis, and operational support, with an active AI program and plans to amplify investments in 2026, though no customer-facing AI products have shipped and no specific revenue or cost savings have been quantified [3]. Market Share (2/2): Arc'teryx is the fastest-growing premium outdoor apparel brand globally, Salomon holds trail running category leadership, and Wilson maintains dominant tennis equipment share; Q2 2026 Asia Pacific revenue surged 60% with Greater China +36%, demonstrating brand power in the world's second-largest consumer market [1]. Product Pipeline (1/2): Continuous product development with FY2026 guidance raised to ~24% revenue growth and Q3 guided at 18-20% growth, though specific next-generation product launches are not individually detailed beyond ongoing brand cadence [1][2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Product innovation is core to each brand's identity with Arc'teryx and Salomon investing in materials science and performance technology above sporting goods industry norms [3].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Amer Sports' purpose of 'elevating the world through sport' is clear and identifies what the company does, but lacks the transformative depth of a truly distinctive cause — interchangeable among premium sporting goods peers [3]. Community Impact (1/2): ISS ESG 'Prime' rating (January 2026), Sustainalytics Industry ESG Risk Leader Badge (score 10.7), and A- CDP Climate rating maintained for two consecutive years demonstrate institutional commitment to sustainability [3][5]. However, the September 2025 Arc'teryx fireworks incident in Tibet — staging fireworks at 5,500 meters in a fragile high-altitude ecosystem — drew boycott calls and a Chinese investigation, undermining the brand's environmental credibility [5]. Employee Retention (1/2): CEO James Zheng has served since 2020 with stable brand-level leaders (Stuart Haselden at Arc'teryx, Guillaume Meyzenq at Salomon, Carrie Ask at Wilson), providing consistent strategic direction across the portfolio. Brand CEO inclusion on the Executive Committee signals organizational trust [2]. Insider Buying (0/2): Significant net insider selling in 2026 — CEO Zheng sold $17.2M in shares and CFO Andrew Page sold $3.9M, with no insider purchases identified, signaling leadership views the current valuation as full.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock with strong metrics across most dimensions. D/E of approximately 16% is well below the 70% target (score 1.0) [4]. ROE of approximately 9.2% is below the 15% target (score 0.61, 2x weight). Revenue growth YoY of 32% far exceeds the 10% target (score 1.0) with Q2 2026 at $1.63B, Q1 at $1.945B, and all segments posting double-digit gains [1][2]. 5yr revenue CAGR of approximately 20% exceeds the 10% target (score 1.0, 2x weight). Forward P/E of approximately 21.4x is slightly above the 20 target (score 0.97). Profit margin of approximately 7.4% is below the 20% target (score 0.37), reflecting the investment-heavy growth phase with DTC expansion and Asia Pacific scaling. Forward PEG of approximately 0.87 is excellent (score 1.0, 2x weight). Q2 2026 adjusted gross margin of 65.8% expanded 710 bps YoY, partly aided by $64.3M in tariff refunds [1]. Daily dollar volume of approximately $184M easily clears the liquidity threshold.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Amer Sports operates in physical sporting goods — designing, manufacturing, and retailing technical apparel (Arc'teryx), footwear (Salomon), and equipment (Wilson) that AI cannot substitute [1]. The DTC channel growth to 55% of revenue relies on physical store expansion and experiential retail immune to AI displacement. No analysts have flagged AI as a substitution risk for premium sporting goods. Brand equity built on decades of materials science and performance credibility cannot be digitally replicated. Some moderate exposure exists through e-commerce channels where AI-powered competitors optimize pricing and personalization, and AI-driven demand forecasting by fast-fashion competitors could pressure trend-sensitive product lines [3]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Amer Sports deploys AI internally for demand planning, content generation, and inventory optimization, but does not generate customer-facing AI revenue or quantifiable AI-derived income streams.

infinite_game.summary: Amer Sports under CEO Zheng and the ANTA consortium has demonstrated commitment to long-term brand building, maintaining premium pricing discipline through tariff disruption and investing heavily in DTC expansion. The brand-level autonomy structure with CEOs for Arc'teryx, Salomon, and Wilson elevated to the Executive Committee reflects genuine organizational trust. However, significant insider selling by the CEO ($17.2M) and CFO ($3.9M), the Arc'teryx fireworks controversy in Tibet, and ANTA's controlling ownership create tension between infinite-minded brand building and finite governance dynamics.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Elevating the world through sport' connects the portfolio brands to enabling athletic achievement and outdoor exploration, shaping strategy: Arc'teryx prioritizes performance over fashion, Salomon invests in trail running community building, Wilson partners with athletes globally [3]. However, the cause hasn't been tested across decades of consistent public market execution — the company IPO'd in 2024, the September 2025 Arc'teryx Tibet fireworks incident contradicted the environmental sustainability narrative [5], and the previous Finnish conglomerate had a different identity.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Each brand operates with significant independence under experienced leaders (Haselden at Arc'teryx, Meyzenq at Salomon, Ask at Wilson), and the expanded Executive Committee structure empowers brand-level decision-making [2]. CEO Zheng's 6+ year tenure provides stability. However, the ANTA consortium's 52% controlling stake and appointment of ANTA executive Wei Lin to the board introduces external governance dynamics that may constrain autonomous decision-making [3].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Amer Sports competes against The North Face, Patagonia, Nike, and adidas across segments, and its competitive language consistently focuses on product differentiation and 'brand-led excellence' rather than defeating rivals [1][3]. Management frames competition as motivation to sharpen distinctive brand identities through superior product innovation rather than engaging in market share warfare.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): The ANTA-led transformation of Arc'teryx from niche mountaineering to mainstream luxury-outdoor and Salomon's pivot from ski hardware to trail running softgoods represent meaningful business model evolution, with DTC reaching 55% of revenue versus a predominantly wholesale model pre-acquisition [1][2]. However, these pivots were enabled by private ownership capital rather than public market courage, and the company has not faced a true existential test as a public company.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Amer Sports maintained premium pricing discipline through tariff disruption rather than discounting, and the Q2 2026 gross margin expansion to 65.8% (+710 bps) demonstrates brand-over-earnings commitment [1]. Management invested aggressively in DTC expansion and Asia Pacific scaling while raising guidance in each of the last four quarters. However, these investments are funded by strong momentum rather than representing costly sacrifice — the company has not yet faced choosing between investment and shareholder returns under true financial pressure.

investment_thesis: Amer Sports at $30.28 with a $17.6B market cap is executing one of the most compelling brand-building stories in global sporting goods, with Q2 2026 revenue surging 32% YoY to $1.63B and adjusted gross margin expanding 710 bps to 65.8% [1]. Arc'teryx continues as the breakout driver, Salomon crossed $2B in annual sales, and DTC reached a record 55% of Q2 revenue. At an estimated PEG of ~0.87 on a forward P/E of ~21.4x, the stock offers rare growth-at-a-reasonable-price among premium consumer brands. FY2026 guidance was raised to ~24% revenue growth with adjusted EPS of $1.27-$1.30, implying ~$8.14B revenue [1][2]. Asia Pacific revenue surged 60% in Q2 with Greater China up 36%, leveraging ANTA's strategic distribution advantage in the world's second-largest consumer market. Q3 2026 is guided at 18-20% revenue growth, maintaining strong momentum.
thesis_continued: The primary risks center on governance, insider selling, and growth sustainability. CEO Zheng sold $17.2M in shares and CFO Page sold $3.9M in 2026, with no insider purchases — meaningful conviction concerns for a stock at ~32x trailing earnings [4]. The ANTA consortium's 52% controlling stake creates governance asymmetry, and the appointment of ANTA executive Wei Lin heightens related-party concerns. The $64.3M tariff refund that boosted Q2 gross margin is a one-time benefit creating tough comparisons for future quarters. ROE of 9.2% and profit margin of 7.4% remain well below targets, reflecting the ongoing investment phase. The September 2025 Arc'teryx fireworks incident in Tibet drew boycott calls and a Chinese government investigation, damaging the brand's environmental credibility in its largest growth market [5]. Heavy Asia Pacific exposure (60% Q2 growth) introduces geopolitical and consumer sentiment concentration risk. The stock's decline from the 200-day average of $34.11 despite strong operational results suggests the market already prices in execution and governance risk.
key_catalysts: Asia Pacific revenue acceleration — Q2 2026 growth of 60% with Greater China up 36% indicates a long runway for premium outdoor brand penetration, leveraging ANTA's distribution expertise in the world's second-largest consumer market [1]
DTC mix expansion toward 60%+ of revenue driving sustained margin improvement as Amer Sports captures more brand premium through owned retail and e-commerce versus wholesale channels [1]

Adjusted operating margin expansion from 12.8% in Q2 toward the mid-teens long-term target as brand scale, DTC penetration, and supply chain optimization compound — FY2026 guided at 14.2-14.5% operating margin with room for further improvement [1][2]
key_risks: Macro sensitivity to consumer discretionary spending — premium outdoor apparel and sporting goods face demand compression in downturns, and the ~32x trailing PE provides limited downside cushion if growth decelerates from the 30%+ pace [4]

ANTA Sports majority ownership creates governance asymmetry; CEO and CFO insider selling totaling $21.1M in 2026 with no purchases signals leadership views the current valuation as full; Arc'teryx Tibet fireworks controversy (September 2025) damaged brand credibility and sparked a Chinese government investigation [4][5]

Tariff policy and trade volatility — while the IEEPA ruling provided a $64.3M Q2 refund, future trade policy changes could reverse this tailwind, and Q3 guidance of 18-20% growth already decelerates from 32% Q2 pace, raising questions about sustainability [1]
